title: British India: the Company and the Raj
subtitle: From a London trading company to Independence · 1600 – 1947
subject: company-rule
intro: Chartered in London in 1600 to trade spices, the East India Company spent its first 150 years as one of several European traders at the edges of the Mughal world. Plassey (1757) and Buxar (1764) made it the ruler of Bengal, and over the next century it defeated Mysore, the Marathas and the Sikhs. After the revolt of 1857 the British Crown took over, ruling through a Viceroy until 1947 — decades that brought famines, railways and English education, and a national movement from the early Congress through Tilak and Gandhi to the Indian National Army. Independence came with the partition of India.

lanes.label: Indian powers, society & the wider world

members.note: Governor-General; became the first Viceroy in 1858

events.title: William Hawkins at Surat
events.summary: The Company's captain William Hawkins lands at Surat and travels to Agra to seek trading rights from Jahangir.

events.title: Bombay in a royal dowry
events.summary: Portugal hands Bombay to Charles II as part of Catherine of Braganza's dowry; he leases it to the Company seven years later.

events.title: Fort William begun
events.summary: The Company starts fortifying its Calcutta settlement as Fort William.

events.title: Siege of Arcot
events.summary: Robert Clive seizes Arcot and holds it for fifty days, turning the Carnatic war against the French.

events.title: Battle of Wandiwash
events.summary: Eyre Coote defeats the French under Lally; French power in India is broken.

events.title: Tipu Sultan killed at Srirangapatna
events.summary: The Company storms Tipu's capital; he dies at the gate, ending the Anglo-Mysore wars.

events.title: Battle of Delhi
events.summary: Lake defeats Shinde's army outside Delhi; the Mughal emperor passes under British protection.

events.title: Vellore mutiny
events.summary: Sepoys at Vellore rise against new dress rules, a rehearsal for 1857.

events.title: Battle of Koregaon
events.summary: A small Company force with many Mahar soldiers holds Koregaon against the Peshwa's army.

events.title: Sindh conquered
events.summary: Charles Napier defeats the Amirs of Sindh at Miani and the province is annexed.

events.title: Awadh annexed
events.summary: Dalhousie annexes Awadh for 'misgovernment' and exiles Nawab Wajid Ali Shah to Calcutta.

events.title: Mangal Pandey at Barrackpore
events.summary: Sepoy Mangal Pandey attacks his officers over the new greased cartridges; he is hanged on 8 April.

events.title: Rani Lakshmibai killed at Gwalior
events.summary: The Rani of Jhansi dies fighting at Gwalior; Tatya Tope fights on until his capture in 1859.

events.title: Vernacular Press Act
events.summary: Lytton's government muzzles the Indian-language press.

events.title: The Ilbert Bill
events.summary: Ripon's proposal to let Indian judges try Europeans meets furious European protest and is watered down.

events.title: Rowlatt Act
events.summary: Wartime powers of detention without trial are extended; Gandhi calls a nationwide hartal.

events.title: Chauri Chaura
events.summary: A crowd burns a police station at Chauri Chaura, killing 22 policemen; Gandhi calls off non-cooperation.

events.title: Gandhi–Irwin Pact
events.summary: Civil disobedience is suspended and prisoners released; Gandhi agrees to attend the Round Table Conference in London.

events.title: Congress wins the provincial elections
events.summary: Under the 1935 Act Congress forms governments in most provinces; the Muslim League does poorly.

events.title: The Cabinet Mission
events.summary: British ministers arrive with a plan for a united federal India; it collapses over the grouping of provinces.

events.title: The partition plan
events.summary: Mountbatten announces that India will be divided and power transferred by August.

events.title: Royal charter
events.summary: Elizabeth I grants a group of London merchants a monopoly on English trade east of the Cape of Good Hope. The East India Company's early target is the spice trade of the East Indies, not India.

events.title: Battle of Swally — a foothold at Surat
events.summary: Company ships defeat a Portuguese squadron off Surat. Jahangir's court, impressed, allows the English a factory (trading post) at Surat, the Mughal empire's chief port.

events.title: Sir Thomas Roe at Jahangir's court
events.summary: James I's ambassador spends four years following the Mughal court to secure better trading terms. The Company is still a petitioner, one trader among many.

events.title: Amboyna: pushed out of the spice islands
events.summary: The Dutch execute English traders at Amboyna in the Moluccas. Squeezed out of the spice trade, the Company turns to Indian cotton textiles, indigo and saltpetre.

events.title: Madras and Fort St. George
events.summary: Under a grant issued in the name of the Vijayanagara emperor, Francis Day acquires a strip of the Coromandel coast. Fort St. George is completed in 1644 and the town of Madras grows around it.

events.title: Bombay leased to the Company
events.summary: Bombay, which came to Charles II in 1661 as part of Catherine of Braganza's dowry from Portugal, is leased to the Company for £10 a year. It replaces Surat — raided twice by Shivaji — as the Company's west coast base.

events.title: Child's War — defeat by the Mughals
events.summary: Under governor Sir Josiah Child the Company attacks Mughal shipping and ports. Aurangzeb's forces besiege Bombay and seize Company factories; the English must beg for pardon and pay a fine. Military conquest is shelved for half a century.

events.title: Job Charnock at Sutanuti — Calcutta
events.summary: Job Charnock re-establishes the Company's Bengal trading post at Sutanuti on the Hooghly. In 1698 the Company buys the rights to three villages — Sutanuti, Gobindapur and Kalikata — and builds Fort William: the beginnings of Calcutta.

events.title: Farrukhsiyar's farman
events.summary: The emperor Farrukhsiyar grants the Company duty-free trade in Bengal. Abuse of these privileges by Company servants trading privately becomes a long-running grievance of the Bengal nawabs.

events.title: Carnatic Wars with the French
events.summary: The British and French companies, under Dupleix on the French side, fight through Indian allies for control of the Carnatic. Robert Clive makes his name defending Arcot (1751); the French are decisively beaten at Wandiwash (1760).

events.title: Siraj-ud-Daulah takes Calcutta
events.summary: The young Nawab of Bengal, angered by fortification work and trade abuses, captures Calcutta. British prisoners die overnight in a cramped guardroom — the 'Black Hole', whose death toll was later greatly exaggerated in British accounts.

events.title: Battle of Plassey
events.summary: Clive retakes Calcutta and, having secretly agreed to make the Nawab's commander Mir Jafar the new nawab, defeats Siraj-ud-Daulah at Plassey when much of the Nawab's army stays out of the fight. The Company becomes kingmaker in India's richest province.

events.title: Battle of Buxar
events.summary: Mir Qasim, the nawab who tried to curb Company abuses, allies with Shuja-ud-Daula of Awadh and Emperor Shah Alam II. The Company defeats all three.

events.title: The Diwani of Bengal
events.summary: By the Treaty of Allahabad, Shah Alam II grants the Company the right to collect the land revenue of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa. Bengal's revenue now pays for the Company's trade and armies.

events.title: Anglo-Mysore Wars
events.summary: Hyder Ali and his son Tipu Sultan, with modernised armies and rockets, fight four wars against the Company. Hyder reaches the outskirts of Madras (1769); Tipu is killed when Srirangapatna is stormed in 1799.

events.title: Great Bengal famine
events.summary: Drought, harsh revenue collection and hoarding combine in a famine that kills perhaps a third of Bengal's population — estimates run to many millions.

events.title: Regulating Act; Warren Hastings Governor-General
events.summary: Parliament begins to oversee the Company. Warren Hastings, governor of Bengal, becomes the first Governor-General, with authority over Madras and Bombay.

events.title: First Anglo-Maratha War
events.summary: The Company backs Raghunathrao's claim to be Peshwa and is defeated at Wadgaon (1779). The Treaty of Salbai restores the pre-war position.

events.title: Pitt's India Act
events.summary: A government Board of Control in London is set over the Company's directors: the start of dual Company–Crown government of India.

events.title: Impeachment of Warren Hastings
events.summary: Edmund Burke leads the impeachment of Hastings for corruption and abuse of power in a seven-year trial that becomes a public debate over the Company's conduct. Hastings is acquitted.

events.title: Permanent Settlement
events.summary: Lord Cornwallis fixes Bengal's land revenue in perpetuity with zamindars, creating a landlord class loyal to British rule while leaving cultivators exposed.

events.title: Wellesley's expansion
events.summary: Governor-General Richard Wellesley uses subsidiary alliances — Hyderabad 1798, the Peshwa at Bassein 1802 — and wars against Mysore and the Marathas. His brother Arthur wins at Assaye; the Company takes Delhi and the Mughal emperor under its protection.

events.title: End of the trade monopoly
events.summary: The Charter Act of 1813 ends the Company's monopoly of trade with India (keeping tea and China) and allows missionaries in. The Company is becoming a government more than a business.

events.title: Third Anglo-Maratha War — the Peshwa falls
events.summary: The last Peshwa, Bajirao II, is defeated and exiled; the Holkars, Shindes and Bhonsles become subordinate princely states. The Company is now the paramount power in India.

events.title: First Anglo-Burmese War
events.summary: A costly war in the east adds Assam, Manipur and Arakan to Company territory.

events.title: Sati abolished
events.summary: Governor-General William Bentinck outlaws sati in Bengal, after years of campaigning by reformers such as Ram Mohan Roy.

events.title: The Company stops trading
events.summary: The Charter Act of 1833 ends the Company's remaining commercial activities. It becomes purely an administrator of India on behalf of the Crown; the Governor-General of Bengal becomes Governor-General of India.

events.title: English education
events.summary: After Macaulay's notorious minute dismissing Indian learning, the Company directs its education funding to teaching in English — creating the English-educated class that later leads the nationalist movement.

events.title: First Anglo-Afghan War
events.summary: An invasion to install a friendly ruler in Kabul ends in the destruction of the retreating British-Indian army in January 1842.

events.title: Anglo-Sikh Wars — Punjab annexed
events.summary: After Ranjit Singh's death (1839) the Sikh Empire weakens. Two hard-fought wars end with the annexation of the Punjab in 1849; the boy maharaja Duleep Singh is exiled to Britain.

events.title: Dalhousie's annexations
events.summary: Under the Doctrine of Lapse Dalhousie annexes states whose rulers die without natural heirs — Satara (1848), Jhansi (1853), Nagpur (1854) — and in 1856 annexes Awadh for 'misgovernment', deposing Wajid Ali Shah.

events.title: The Phules' school for girls in Pune
events.summary: Jyotirao and Savitribai Phule open one of the first schools for girls run by Indians, in Pune — the start of their lifelong work against caste and gender discrimination.

events.title: First passenger train
events.summary: India's first passenger train runs from Bombay to Thane. Railways and the telegraph spread rapidly under Dalhousie.

events.title: Revolt of 1857
events.summary: After Mangal Pandey's attack on officers at Barrackpore in March, sepoys mutiny at Meerut and march to Delhi, proclaiming Bahadur Shah Zafar emperor. The uprising spreads across north India — Kanpur, Lucknow, Jhansi — led by figures such as Nana Sahib, Rani Lakshmibai and Tatya Tope, and is crushed with great brutality.

events.title: The Crown takes over
events.summary: The Government of India Act transfers the Company's territories, army and powers to the British Crown. The Governor-General becomes Viceroy.

events.title: Queen Victoria's Proclamation
events.summary: Lord Canning, the first Viceroy, reads Queen Victoria's proclamation at Allahabad: the Crown takes over from the East India Company, promises not to interfere in religion, and abandons annexation of the princely states.

events.title: The Indian Civil Service
events.summary: Recruited by examination held in London, the ICS becomes the 'steel frame' of British rule. Satyendranath Tagore becomes its first Indian member in 1864; the London-only exam keeps Indians a small minority for decades.

events.title: Gandhi born at Porbandar
events.summary: Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi is born in Porbandar, Gujarat. The Suez Canal opens the same year, bringing India much closer to Britain.

events.title: Satyashodhak Samaj
events.summary: In Pune, Jyotirao Phule founds the Satyashodhak Samaj (Society of Truth-seekers) to challenge caste hierarchy and Brahmin dominance.

events.title: The Company is dissolved
events.summary: With its remaining dividend obligations paid off, the East India Company is formally wound up.

events.title: The Great Famine
events.summary: Drought across south and west India turns into a famine killing millions, while grain exports continue and relief is kept deliberately meagre. It is the first of several devastating late-19th-century famines.

events.title: Victoria proclaimed Empress of India
events.summary: At the Delhi Durbar of 1877, held while famine raged in the south, Queen Victoria is proclaimed Kaisar-i-Hind, Empress of India.

events.title: Indian National Congress founded
events.summary: Seventy-two delegates meet in Bombay, encouraged by the retired official A. O. Hume. Early leaders like Dadabhai Naoroji — whose 'drain of wealth' theory indicts British economic policy — petition for reform within the empire.

events.title: Vivekananda at Chicago
events.summary: Swami Vivekananda's address to the World's Parliament of Religions makes him famous and becomes a source of national self-confidence.

events.title: Plague in Pune: the Chapekar brothers kill Rand
events.summary: Harsh plague-control measures in Pune — forced house searches and removals — lead the Chapekar brothers to shoot the plague commissioner W. C. Rand. Tilak, whose newspaper Kesari had denounced the measures, is jailed for sedition.

events.title: Partition of Bengal and the Swadeshi movement
events.summary: Viceroy Curzon divides Bengal along largely religious lines. The protest movement boycotts British goods (Swadeshi) and turns nationalism into a mass cause.

events.title: All-India Muslim League founded
events.summary: Muslim leaders meeting at Dhaka found the Muslim League to represent Muslim interests; the 1909 reforms give it separate electorates.

events.title: Congress splits at Surat
events.summary: The Congress session at Surat breaks up in chaos as the Moderates, led by Gokhale, and the Extremists, led by Tilak, Lala Lajpat Rai and Bipin Chandra Pal, part ways.

events.title: Tilak sentenced to Mandalay
events.summary: Tilak is convicted of sedition and spends six years in prison at Mandalay in Burma, where he writes the Gita Rahasya.

events.title: Capital moves to Delhi
events.summary: At the Delhi Durbar, George V announces that the capital will move from Calcutta to Delhi and that the partition of Bengal is annulled. New Delhi is inaugurated in 1931.

events.title: First World War
events.summary: More than a million Indian soldiers serve overseas — in France, Mesopotamia, East Africa and Gallipoli — and over 70,000 die. Indian leaders expect self-government in return.

events.title: Gandhi returns from South Africa
events.summary: After two decades leading the Indian community's struggle in South Africa, Gandhi returns to India, travels widely on Gokhale's advice, and founds an ashram at Ahmedabad.

events.title: Home Rule and the Lucknow Pact
events.summary: Tilak and Annie Besant launch Home Rule Leagues — 'Swaraj is my birthright, and I shall have it'. At Lucknow the Congress and the Muslim League agree a joint scheme for reform.

events.title: Jallianwala Bagh massacre
events.summary: In Amritsar, after protests against the repressive Rowlatt Act, General Reginald Dyer orders troops to fire without warning on a crowd in an enclosed garden, killing hundreds. It turns much of India against British rule.

events.title: Non-cooperation movement
events.summary: On the day Tilak dies, Gandhi launches non-cooperation: boycott of British goods, schools, courts and titles, alongside the Khilafat movement. After a mob kills policemen at Chauri Chaura in February 1922, Gandhi calls it off.

events.title: Simon Commission boycotted
events.summary: An all-British commission to review the constitution is met with protests of 'Simon, go back'. Lala Lajpat Rai dies after being beaten in a police lathi charge in Lahore.

events.title: Purna Swaraj
events.summary: At Lahore, under Jawaharlal Nehru's presidency, the Congress declares complete independence its goal; 26 January 1930 is celebrated as Independence Day.

events.title: Salt March
events.summary: Gandhi walks 390 km from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi to make salt in defiance of the salt tax, starting a civil disobedience movement in which tens of thousands are jailed.

events.title: Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and Sukhdev hanged
events.summary: The three revolutionaries are executed in Lahore for the killing of a police officer in revenge for Lajpat Rai's death. Rajguru was from Khed near Pune, today renamed Rajgurunagar in his honour.

events.title: Poona Pact
events.summary: Gandhi fasts in Yerawada jail against separate electorates for the Depressed Classes, which Ambedkar had won. Ambedkar agrees to reserved seats within joint electorates instead — a compromise he later criticised.

events.title: Government of India Act 1935
events.summary: Provincial autonomy and a wider franchise; Congress wins most provinces in the 1937 elections. Much of the Act later shapes India's constitution.

events.title: Second World War
events.summary: The Viceroy declares India at war without consulting Indian leaders; Congress ministries resign. About 2.5 million Indians serve in the largest volunteer army in history.

events.title: Lahore Resolution
events.summary: The Muslim League, led by Jinnah, calls for independent states in the Muslim-majority regions — the demand for Pakistan.

events.title: Quit India
events.summary: At Gowalia Tank in Bombay, Gandhi calls on the British to 'Quit India' — 'Do or die'. The Congress leadership is arrested the next morning and a largely leaderless uprising is suppressed.

events.title: Bengal famine
events.summary: Wartime shortages, the loss of Burmese rice, hoarding and government policy produce a famine in which about three million people die.

events.title: Bose and the Indian National Army
events.summary: Subhas Chandra Bose proclaims a Provisional Government of Free India in Singapore and leads the INA alongside Japan. The 1945–46 Red Fort trials of INA officers spark nationwide sympathy.

events.title: Royal Indian Navy mutiny
events.summary: Sailors in Bombay strike and seize ships, joined by thousands across the country — a sign that Britain can no longer count on its Indian forces.

events.title: Direct Action Day — the Calcutta killings
events.summary: A Muslim League call for protest turns into days of communal killing in Calcutta, followed by violence in Noakhali and Bihar. Partition comes to look unavoidable.

events.title: Integration of the princely states
events.summary: Sardar Patel and V. P. Menon bring over 550 princely states — including the Maratha states of Gwalior, Indore, Baroda and Kolhapur — into the Indian Union.

events.title: Independence and Partition
events.summary: Under Mountbatten's plan British India is divided into two dominions, India and Pakistan. Nehru becomes Prime Minister. The partition displaces some 15 million people and is accompanied by killing on a massive scale, with estimates of the dead running from several hundred thousand to two million.

events.title: Gandhi assassinated
events.summary: Gandhi is shot dead in Delhi by Nathuram Godse, a Hindu nationalist.

events.title: India becomes a republic
events.summary: The Constitution, drafted by a committee chaired by B. R. Ambedkar, comes into force — on the anniversary of the 1930 Purna Swaraj day.
